results.fact: Total elevation gain/loss for the route
results.evidence: Sources do not agree on one figure. A detailed trip report of exactly this route (Pete Lake - Chimney Glacier - East Face) gives about 6,000 ft gained and lost and 19 miles, which is where gain_ft, loss_ft, the overview and itinerary.totalNote come from. The Mountaineers route page for the neighbouring East Face Direct gives 4,900 ft and 16 miles; the same trip-report author's South Peak ascent by the same approach gives about 5,000 ft; another party (19.6 mi) logged 8,463 ft. The itinerary day figures (1,850 + 3,080 = 4,930) are just trailhead-to-summit net, which ignores approach undulation, so they are a floor rather than evidence the 6,000 is wrong. No two independent sources agree on a value for this route; no patch.

results.fact: Hardest grade of the summit pitches
results.evidence: The route's own consensus page rates the East Face 5.3 (3 pitches: low-5th chimney, 4th-class slab, low-5th chimney). But the three summit pitches above the Key Ledge are shared with the East Face Direct, whose route page describes several moves of 5.4-5.6 on them and a 5.5 chimney move to gain the summit, and a party that climbed the standard line via the U-Notch called its third pitch awkward and 'probably no more difficult than 5.6'. Two sources lean harder than 5.3 and one says 5.3, so the 5.3 in grade/rock_grade/pitch_detail cannot be confirmed, and the 5.4-5.6 in climbing_route[3] cannot be removed. No patch.

results.fact: Number of rappels on the standard descent
results.evidence: climbing_route[4] reproduces the East Face Direct route page's descent (two rappels summit to Key Ledge, then six to the glacier), which that page offers as one of TWO descents from the Key Ledge; the other is reversing the normal East Face ledges via the notch. Sources for the normal descent disagree with the row's '2 rappels near the bergschrund' in a different way: one trip report made rappels from the summit to the broad ledge on a single 165 ft rope PLUS two rappels near the base, another made three rappels to the Key Ledge plus one from the white rocks. So both the '2 total' fields and the '~8' climbing_route step are wrong in different ways, and the sources do not agree on a single count to adopt. Needs a rewrite of rappels/rappel_detail/descent_text/climbing_route[4] together once a count is settled; no patch.

results.fact: Overall commitment/alpine grade of the route
results.evidence: The consensus route page for the East Face lists a Grade IV commitment (matching alpine_grade and commitment), while the Mountaineers page rates the neighbouring East Face Direct Grade II (the source of climbing_route[3]'s 'Grade II overall'). No second source for either value on the standard East Face; no patch.

results.fact: Name of the notch between the South and Main summits
results.evidence: They are two different features: the U-Gap (U-Notch) is on the south side, reached by a gully from the glacier; the traverse then crosses the east face of the South Peak to the separate notch between the South and Main peaks (the Main Notch). The row's own baseFinding says as much ('Above the U-Gap the traverse across the South Peak toward the Main Peak', then '...downclimbed about fifty feet from the Main Notch').

results.fact: Hardest technical rock grade on the route
results.evidence: No independent description of a 'West Face / South Summit' route on Washington's Chimney Rock could be found; published routes are the East Face, East Face Direct, North Face and North Peak lines. The row's distinctive details (a 'Rappel Chimney', grooves 30-40 ft right of it, a rocking summit block) match the West Face of Chimney Rock in north Idaho, where 'Rappel Chimney' is a named 5.7 route and the most-climbed West Face line is 5.3 — so this record appears to carry another peak's data, and neither 5.6 nor 4th class can be confirmed. The row's own corrections field already flags it for manual review. Whole record needs review; no patch.
